subject.title: Onboarding Wizard should include Memory/Embedding setup as a mandatory step

question: Should first-run onboarding and openclaw configure treat memory embedding setup as mandatory, prominently optional, or diagnostic-only, and what credential/probe UX should it use?
rationale: Current source confirms the setup gap, but the requested mandatory behavior changes first-run friction, provider cost, offline/local workflows, credential storage, and daemon environment expectations.

options.title: Prominent Optional Setup
options.body: Add a visible but skippable memory setup/readiness step that configures existing memorySearch provider/model and API-key or SecretRef fields, then points users to memory status verification.

options.title: Mandatory Memory Gate
options.body: Require users to configure embeddings or explicitly choose FTS-only before onboarding completes, improving recall readiness at the cost of setup friction and provider dependency.

options.title: Diagnostic Only
options.body: Keep onboarding lean and rely on memory status, doctor, and docs, accepting that some users may discover memory readiness only after first use.

recommendation.title: Prominent Optional Setup
recommendation.body: Add a visible but skippable memory setup/readiness step that configures existing memorySearch provider/model and API-key or SecretRef fields, then points users to memory status verification.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman is assigned to this issue and already participated in the product-scope discussion, making them the best available owner for the policy choice.
